# Current state — legeos

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

_(none)_

## Constraints

### The first release does not attempt a custom kernel, libc, package format/manager, display protocol, object filesystem, universal checkpointing, all NVIDIA generations, an app store, phone/tablet/server editions, or third-party shell extensions

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.first-release-scope/1` · scope `all` · topic `first-release-scope`

Until the five first-release claims are proven, LegeOS keeps systemd, cgroup v2, APT/Debian packages, standard filesystems, PipeWire, NetworkManager, BlueZ, Mesa and the upstream NVIDIA userspace stack. It does not build: a Linux kernel fork, a new package format or manager, a new libc/basic userland, replacement networking/Bluetooth/audio stacks, a new display protocol, a semantic/object filesystem replacing paths, transparent checkpointing of arbitrary applications, support for every old NVIDIA generation, a complete alternative application store, phone/tablet/server editions, or extensions/third-party shell plugins.

### Identity comes from the launch cgroup, never from a client's self-declared app_id; Exec= is never run through a shell; the governor is observe-only until traces are reviewed and never selects a victim by memory size alone

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.identity-and-launch-safety/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-appd/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "services/lege-resourced/**"` · topic `identity-launch-governor-safety`

(1) A window's application identity is resolved PID -> cgroup -> instance -> canonical AppId; client claims (Wayland app_id, WM_CLASS, sandbox id) can only lower confidence (claim mismatch) or, when unique, yield claim-only confidence — never override a verified launch, and privileged actions require verified-launch. (2) Applications are launched as the registered executable plus an argument vector in a dedicated systemd unit; Exec= lines are parsed, never passed to a shell. (3) lege-resourced ships observe-only; enforcement (memory.high, reclaim, checkpoint, cgroup.kill) is enabled in stages after recorded traces are reviewed; the victim score weighs growth, PSI contribution, foreground/visible state, unsaved work and disposability, never resident size alone; session-critical units are never candidates.

### Exactly one selected provider per exclusive system role may autostart

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.one-provider-per-role/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-session-core/src/autostart.rs"`, `path "crates/lege-session-core/src/providers.rs"`, `path "crates/lege-types/src/provider.rs"` · topic `one-provider-per-role`

For every ProviderRole (network-status-ui, notification-server, file-chooser, file-manager, lock-screen, association-broker, clipboard-manager, power-manager, screenshot-service, input-method, portal-backend, greeter) installing a second provider never silently starts both; the user or distribution policy selects one and only that one autostarts.

### Every component is a Debian package (nothing under /usr/local or untracked in $HOME); lege-window carries no async runtime or D-Bus dependency

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.packaging-and-render-thread/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "debian/**"`, `path "tools/xtask/**"` · topic `packaging-and-render-thread`

All binaries, units, manifests and policy files are installed by Debian packages (cargo-deb now, the vendored source package later); development installs go through a local apt repository. The compositor-side lege-window crate must never depend on tokio, zbus, async-std or smol because it runs on the compositor render thread.

### System behaviour belongs in services; tray icons, panels and applets are views

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.services-not-indicators/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-session-core/**"`, `path "services/**"`, `path "shell/**"` · topic `services-not-indicators`

No policy (timezone discovery, power decisions, autostart choices, association defaults, notification storage) is implemented in a shell surface or applet; each lives in a service crate/daemon with a D-Bus interface, and the shell only renders and forwards user choices.

## Observations

### A Trash1 smoke test run against the real session bus emptied the user's actual volume trash

`verified` · `@legeos.observation.agent-smoke-test-emptied-a-real-volume-trash/1` · scope `path "cli/lege/**"`, `path "services/lege-filed/**"`

While smoke-testing `lege trash empty --yes` end to end, the implementing agent constructed TrashApi with TrashMounts::System instead of TrashMounts::Fixed, so the sweep read the machine's real mount table, found /media/dk/4668959A68958977/.Trash-1000, and permanently deleted its one entry — a folder named `target` (a Rust build directory, regenerable) trashed on 2026-08-30. Unrecoverable. The code behaved as designed; the harness choice was the fault: TrashMounts::Fixed exists precisely so tests cannot reach real disks, every committed test uses it, and the offending smoke script was removed rather than left as a trap. Standing rule going forward: any end-to-end exercise of destructive file operations must run against fixture mounts (TrashMounts::Fixed, a throwaway HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME) — never the developer host's real mount table.

### Third hands-on run at the installed desktop: Files object inert by pointer, band over client content, no window controls, no resize route

`verified` · `@legeos.observation.hands-on-run-3-findings-20260903/1` · scope `path "apps/lege-files/**"`, `path "compositor/lege-comp/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"`

User logged into the LegeOS desktop at cb57689 (installed packages match HEAD) to test in-place hot-fixing and reports: (1) redundant HOME labels on the left of the file manager; (2) Copy path does nothing and no button in the file manager works; (3) a bare Super press hides windows but not the open file manager; (4) windows have no minimize or close buttons; (5) Kitty's top line is cut off by the window pane; (6) windows move but do not resize. Usability otherwise possible but poor. Diagnosis from the code: the 'file manager' is the shell's expanded Files object on Home (Layer::HomeSurface), so a reveal never hides it and its rail read Home ▸ Home over PLACE Home; single click activated rows, so the selection-gated file verbs stayed inert; spawn_copy_path rendered the text and never put it on a clipboard; the compositor painted its 32 px recovery band OVER the client's top strip (hiding client-side close buttons and a terminal's first line) and offered only a 24 px corner grip for resizing.

### Why the Home Field failed at a real desktop: four typing defects, an inverted rung rule, an unregistered interface and a mixed-age install

`verified` · `@legeos.observation.home-hands-on-failures-diagnosed/1` · scope `path "apps/lege-greeter/**"`, `path "compositor/lege-comp/**"`, `path "services/lege-sessiond/**"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"`

A desktop tester reported that typing was slow and error-prone, that there was no logout control, and that the shutdown control was always visible and did nothing. Every cause was located and none was a regression; all were present in a workspace-green tree.

Typing, four independent defects. (1) Both winit surfaces translated a key press with `.chars().next()`, but `Key::Character` carries a `SmolStr` because a dead-key or compose commit with no precomposed form arrives as base letter plus combining mark in one event — the remainder was dropped silently (shell/lege-shell/src/surface/window.rs:125 and the identical copy in apps/lege-greeter/src/surface/window.rs, where the field is a password). (2) The compositor asked for `XkbConfig::default()` — empty rules/model/layout/variant and `options: None` — so no configured layout was honoured and no Compose key existed (compositor/lege-comp/src/state.rs:205). (3) `ensure_launcher_icons` ran on the winit event-loop thread on every redraw, and every accepted key requests a redraw: each miss read .desktop files across every XDG_DATA_DIRS entry, stat-ed a candidate per size bucket per extension per theme directory, then decoded a PNG or rasterized an SVG at 128x128, between a key press and the frame showing its character (shell/lege-shell/src/surface/app.rs:501, shell/lege-shell/src/icons.rs:241-367). (4) Full repaint and full-buffer present per keystroke with no damage tracking, which sets the latency floor the third defect then exceeds. `pixelkit_shell::Input` holds `keys` as a Vec, so no key is dropped by queueing.

Power controls. The session widget declared `session.lock` and `session.poweroff` at `Representation::Small` and `session.logout` at `Wide` (shell/lege-shell/src/surface/widgets/mod.rs:102-108), while a system tile is created at its floor span and stays there (shell/lege-shell/src/field_model.rs:227) — so on every real desktop the destructive action was the one that could not be hidden and the safe one was behind a resize the default density makes inert. Separately, `Session.Lifecycle1` was registered only if the system-bus connection had succeeded at sessiond startup, with no retry, unlike `Location1` two lines above (services/lege-sessiond/src/main.rs:388-409, 552-564): losing that race removed every power control for the whole session. Every failure path in the shell's `spawn_lifecycle` was a `tracing::error!` and nothing on screen, and `draw_region_strip` never consulted logind's Can* verdicts, so a control known to be refused was drawn identically to a working one.

Install coherence. The installed set was mixed-age: ten of thirteen LegeOS packages were more than a day older than lege-shell, so a 2026-08-25 shell was calling interfaces and protocol requests that the 2026-08-22 sessiond and 2026-08-23 compositor predate.

### Home's three-second refresh profiled: what was fixed, and the two service-side costs that remain

`verified` · `@legeos.observation.home-refresh-costs-profiled-20260902/1` · scope `path "services/lege-sessiond/src/apis/audio.rs"`, `path "services/lege-sessiond/src/apis/lifecycle.rs"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"`

Measured against a live sessiond on the development host, one pass of the Home Surface's three-second refresh loop cost about 82ms, of which: fetch_apps 34ms, fetch_settings_widget 19ms, fetch_session_widget 18ms, fetch_all(20) 5.5ms, fetch_projects 2.6ms, fetch_browser_sources 0.8ms. Separately, zbus's Connection::session() builds a new connection — socket, SASL handshake, Hello and a reader task — on every call, and the shell called it from three dozen places; caching one connection per tokio runtime took fetch_all from 14ms to 5.5ms.

Fixed in 392bd0d and f148046: the connection cache, joining the loop's independent fetches, joining the Session widget's three logind Can* questions (18ms to 13ms), and moving the application-catalogue read onto AppIdentity1.ApplicationsChanged plus a thirty-second backstop. An ordinary tick is now about 27ms.

Two costs remain and both are inside lege-sessiond, not the shell. Audio1.Get spawns `wpctl` as a child process on every call, which is most of fetch_settings_widget's remaining time; the Home Settings widget therefore spawns a process every three seconds for as long as the session lasts. Lifecycle1's Can* answers still cost about 13ms even when the three are asked together, which suggests the system-bus round trips to logind are being serialised inside sessiond rather than by the caller; logind's answer to whether this machine may shut down does not change between two three-second ticks and is a candidate for caching.

### Omarchy launches applications into transient systemd units too, then identifies windows by self-declared app_id anyway

`verified` · `@legeos.observation.transient-unit-launch-converged-independently/2` · scope `path "crates/lege-appd/**"`, `path "crates/lege-types/**"`

Basecamp's Omarchy independently arrived at the same launch primitive LegeOS uses: bin/omarchy-launch-browser and five sibling scripts start applications with `systemd-run --user --collect --unit="omarchy-browser-$(date +%s%N)"`, giving one transient unit and therefore one cgroup per launch. It then does not use it. There is no reference to a cgroup, a unit or /proc/<pid>/cgroup anywhere under shell/; the shell identifies windows purely from the client's self-declared app_id (12 references). The cgroup exists and the information is discarded. This sharpens what LegeOS's identity model actually contributes: not that a per-launch cgroup exists, but that naming it app-legeos-<AppId>@<InstanceId>.service makes the cgroup name carry the identity, so a window's PID resolves to a cgroup, the cgroup name resolves to an AppId, and the governor, the dock and the notification router all key off one fact nobody had to ask the client for. Omarchy's unit name is a timestamp and carries no identity, so it cannot make that journey even though it has the cgroup. Independent convergence on the primitive is evidence the primitive is right; the naming convention is the part that turns it into an identity system, and is the part to defend in review.

**supersedes** `@legeos.observation.transient-unit-launch-converged-independently/1`

### Undoing a trash restored nothing and still committed — and the covering test hid it by substituting its own inputs

`verified` · `@legeos.observation.trash-undo-reported-a-restore-it-did-not-perform/1` · scope `path "services/lege-filed/**"`

Undo of a trash operation reported success and moved no file. undo_of built the undo plan from the operation's own paths — the pre-trash locations, the only ones OperationKind::Trash retains — so plan emitted Step::RestoreFromTrash aimed at a path the file had just vacated; execute found nothing there, took that for 'already restored', returned Ok, and the operation reached Committed. Ctrl+Z in the Files app and lege files undo both told the user the file was back when it was still in the trash. The same defect existed in the other direction, undoing a restore, with no test coverage at all.

What matters beyond the fix: the test that should have caught this concealed it. trashing_and_undoing_it_round_trip took undo_of's result, discarded its paths, looked the real trashed paths up itself via trash::list, and passed those in — a substitution production never performs. The test therefore exercised a path no caller takes and passed for four months while the production path was broken. A test that repairs its subject's output before asserting on it is not covering that subject; the repair is the bug, made invisible.

Fixed at git:464e069b7b2769bc5e0ab34e8191b65f9101e7db by recording where the trash actually put each item into the executed step, the way Move's undo already reads its RenameInPlace destination. A post-hoc trash::list lookup could not serve: trash::free_name resolves collisions against the live directory, so a path trashed twice leaves two records and nothing outside the operation can say which is which. The corrected test feeds undo_of straight into plan; reverting the fix fails it.

## Assessments

### Desktop test-readiness audit — strong logic tests, missing system validation and core interaction surfaces

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.desktop-test-readiness-20260827/1` · scope `path "apps/**"`, `path "ci/**"`, `path "compositor/**"`, `path "portals/**"`, `path "scripts/**"`, `path "services/**"`, `path "shell/**"`, `path "tests/**"`

LegeOS has a large, currently green unit/property test base, but the desktop cannot yet be considered system-tested: the integration harness does not start or drive a real composed session, the documented hardware runner is inert, installation/greeter/recovery/hardware paths remain manual, and several ordinary desktop interactions still have no graphical implementation.

- `#accessibility-and-localisation` — The repository ships accessibility and localisation intentions, but no AT-SPI/accessibility-tree implementation or runtime Fluent loader is present in the audited sources.
- `#automated-foundation` — All 1,015 workspace tests, lint/format checks, runtime smoke, and seven structural/action gates pass on the audited working tree.
- `#desktop-capability-gaps` — Graphical Settings is still a text renderer; FileChooser, AppChooser and Background portal prompts use NoUiAvailable; session lock is NotSupported; notifications are stored but not rendered; and power profiles are stored without idle/lid/brightness/battery actuation.
- `#false-green-risks` — The smoke test imports developer-host application state and tolerates an UNHEALTHY boot-health report, Home's offscreen test checks PNG validity and dimensions rather than rendered pixels, CI builds only the sessiond Debian package, and compositor-active boot health is explicitly unwired.
- `#hardware-runner-noop` — `lege doctor --hardware` produces byte-identical output to ordinary doctor because Context.hardware is never consumed; tests/hardware/*.toml is currently passive checklist data.
- `#system-test-gap` — There is no automated greetd-to-Home login, nested compositor input/render interaction, installed multi-package session, VM first-boot, shell-death recovery, or real-hardware execution path.

### Home Field usability audit — a deliberate divergence is a gap only where its substitute is missing, weaker or undiscoverable

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.home-field-usability-gaps-20260831/1` · scope `path "apps/**"`, `path "compositor/**"`, `path "portals/**"`, `path "services/lege-filed/**"`, `path "shell/**"`

Audited the Home Field and the modules around it against mainstream desktop expectations. The Home Field's rejections — no taskbar, no tray, no virtual desktops, no title bars — are the product, so this audit judges each one by its substitute rather than by the convention it dropped, and reports a gap only where the substitute is missing, weaker or undiscoverable. On that test the shell's own rejections mostly hold; what fails is a different class of thing entirely — capabilities the project intends to have, believes it has, or documents as shipped, which are absent in code.

JUDGED BY SUBSTITUTE, AND SOUND. Virtual desktops: rejected by the one-workspace invariant (compositor/COMPOSITOR.md:12); substitute is park-to-tile plus show-all plus Alt-Tab; the substitute is real, but window.park has no chord at all and window.show-all has no pointer route outside one context menu, so the gap is discoverability, not the missing workspaces. Taskbar: rejected; substitute is the field's own app and parked-session tiles, which is a genuine replacement. Tray: rejected under the services-not-indicators constraint; substitute is the widget system plus ProviderRole slots, which works for network via the user's nm-tray2 but leaves a third-party app no place to dock. Title bars: no server-side chrome renderer, so decoration is forced client-side (compositor/lege-comp/src/xdg_shell.rs:467); the substitute for close is a context-menu row and for resize a compositor-painted grip, but there is no user-facing maximize control at all — a window only maximizes if the app asks.

GENUINE GAPS, RANKED BY DAILY COST. (1) No multi-select anywhere: the field carries a single focus: Option<TileId> (shell/lege-shell/src/surface/field_screen.rs:157) and the drawer browser a single entry_focus: usize (surface/file_browser.rs:54); no shift-click, ctrl-click or marquee exists, so no bulk action on files or tiles is possible. (2) Nothing is discoverable: no cheat sheet, tooltip, help overlay or first-run anywhere in the shell; park, close, restore and reset have no chord and live only in a right-click menu the user must guess is there; the action manifest can already generate a cheat sheet and nothing renders one. (3) No file operations from Home: navigate and open only — no rename, copy, move, new folder, properties or clipboard, and no drag of a file into an application; Operation::OpenWith and AddReference return None (field_screen.rs:1435). (4) The trash could not list its contents. (5) Accessibility is claimed but not built.

DOCUMENTED-BUT-ABSENT, which is a distinct and worse category than merely missing, because the docs assert it: docs/architecture/accessibility.md claims AT-SPI support and a high-contrast variant for every shell surface; no atspi dependency exists in any Cargo.toml and no contrast token or theme exists in shell/lege-shell/src. a11y.seed installs Orca with nothing to read, because the shell paints itself with a custom rasterizer and exposes no accessible name, role or state for any tile, row or widget. Reduced motion and the focus ring are real and respected; the rest of the claim is not implemented.

ABSENT WITH NO SUBSTITUTE: Lifecycle1.Lock hard-fails NotSupported although the compositor fully implements ext-session-lock-v1 — nothing drives it; volume, brightness and battery exist nowhere in the tree as code, not as stubs; the Files app has no new folder, search, sort control, view mode or breadcrumbs, though lege-filed supports CreateDirectory; the OpenURI, Screenshot, ScreenCast and Print portals do not exist; no removable-media mount or eject; no display configuration; no keyboard-layout switcher, touchpad settings or IME.

STALE LEDGER CLAIMS corrected by this audit: the graphical settings app and the shell's notification rendering both shipped on 2026-08-30, after the 08-27 readiness audit that called them stubs, and the portal NoUiAvailable path is now a headless-only fallback rather than the default.

### Hot-fixability and daily-development readiness, 2026-08-31

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.hotfixability-current-state-20260831/2` · scope `path "crates/lege-state/**"`, `path "debian/**"`, `path "distro/**"`, `path "docs/planning/**"`, `path "installer/**"`, `path "packaging/**"`, `path "scripts/reinstall-legeos-desktop.sh"`, `path "services/lege-hostd/**"`, `path "session/units/**"`

LegeOS is currently suitable for active development as an additional desktop session on a stable Ubuntu host with the host session, display manager, TTY and backups retained as recovery paths. Stage-1 packages can be installed while the old session runs; applications, shell and separated services provide progressively restartable activation boundaries, while the compositor honestly requires logout and kernel/driver/boot changes require a staged reboot. It is not yet suitable as the sole recoverable bare-metal daily driver because installer/ISO and clean-install gates are unfinished, boot-deployment rollback is not hardware-proven and ADR-0004 remains open, coordinated service restart and cross-version state/IPC skew are unproven, and the archive path is inconsistent with the Rust 1.97 workspace and still has sibling path dependencies.

## Evidence

### Accessibility documentation corrected to match the code; deferral is now explicit

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.accessibility-docs-honest-20260831/1`

The record's 'correct the documentation' outcome, chosen per the user's standing priority of product gaps over accessibility: docs/architecture/accessibility.md now separates what actually holds (compositor-reachable recovery routes, enforced keyboard/pointer parity via check-actions, manifest-driven help, distinct focus indicator, reduced motion, CLI parity) from what is deliberately deferred and stated as not implemented (no AT-SPI bridge — a screen reader meets a silent desktop; no high-contrast variant), and distro/seeds/README.md stops advertising high-contrast assets while a11y.seed keeps installing the AT stack ready for a future bridge. Building the bridge remains open, honestly labelled, rather than falsely documented.

### One declaration drives the menu, the cheat sheet and the CLI, held together by gates

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.action-manifest-three-surfaces-20260831/1`

The one-declaration mechanism exists and is enforced: lege_types::action::MANIFEST (a shared types crate, not the shell) carries id, human label, chords, cli_verb, confirm and a Requires availability predicate for 38 actions; the Home context menu renders rows by declared id, the F1 help sheet iterates the manifest by category, and every cli_verb is checked to reach a real lege subcommand. check-actions fails the build when a surface performs an undeclared id or a chord lacks a pointer route (the additive-keyboard rule, with the exemption list empty), and a lege-comp test holds the compositor's fixed recovery keysym table in agreement with the manifest's chords.

### Fullscreen stays clean: no arrangement chrome outside Home, fullscreen windows never arranged

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.arrangements-fullscreen-clean-20260831/1`

Fullscreen windows are excluded from arrangement eligibility (WindowService::arrangement_eligible filters window.fullscreen), and the arrangement controls live on the Home Field's secondary-click menu inside the Home surface — no ShellOverlay surface, no exclusive zone, no reserved strip exists for them — so a fullscreen application occupies its output with no arrangement chrome visible, by construction.

### M1: a trial boot can fail because the session never came up

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-boot-health-can-fail/1`

lege-sessiond reports session health to lege-hostd at the moment it signals systemd readiness, so an absent session-healthy marker now means the session did not come up rather than that nobody could report it. The compositor-active marker stays deliberately unwired and reports Skipped, because sessiond has no honest evidence for it; the two switches are separate so arming one never arms the other. A skip never arms a reboot, and only a boot genuinely trialling a candidate can force one.

### M1: the checkpoint protocol is deliverable end to end, and verifies its peer

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-checkpoint-transport/1`

org.legeos.Checkpoint1 is served by an application instance and called by lege-sessiond on the governor's behalf, addressed by a bus name derived from the InstanceId so nothing is registered and no directory goes stale. The daemon resolves the claimed name's PID and confirms its cgroup names that exact instance before believing any answer — an application squatting another instance's name is refused without being called — and every call is bounded by the request's own deadline, so a peer barely responsive under the pressure that prompted the request is refused rather than hanging the relay.

### M1: every service is reachable from the CLI, the portal, the shell and Settings

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-clients-reachable/1`

lege covers app, open (URIs and paths, with the broker's own explanation under --explain), res, files, history with undo, providers, settings, project, power and the whole Host surface; the portal serves FileChooser over the same last-directory answer the file manager uses, plus OpenURI, AppChooser, Settings and Background; lege-shell renders all ten drawers live over D-Bus with dock grouping by canonical AppId; lege-settings serves six pages. Every service-absent path degrades to one sentence naming the service, verified with no bus present. Toolkit-dependent choosers are explicit seam traits that refuse rather than fabricate.

### M1: the governor defaults to observe-only and performs nothing above its stage

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-governor-staged/1`

Stage defaults to observe-only; an action above the current stage is decided, scored, signalled with applied=false and not performed. RestoreDynamicLimits only writes when the governor itself placed the override, so observe-only performs no cgroup write at all with an application present — tested directly. Traces record pressure episodes and level changes rather than idle ticks, so the ring holds episodes rather than wall-clock noise. 62 tests.

**Verifies**

- `completed` `@legeos.milestone.m1-session-runtime/1` — check `governor-staged`

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-operations-resume/1`
